question.body:
At a certain height, a tree trunk has a circular cross section. The radius $R(t)$ of that cross section grows at a rate modeled by the function $ frac(d R,d t)= frac(1,16)lr((3 + sin lr((t^(2))))) " centimeters per year " $ for $0 <= t <= 3$, where time $t$ is measured in years. At time $t = 0$, the radius is 6 centimeters. The area of the cross section at time $t$ is denoted by $A(t)$.

(a) Write an expression, involving an integral, for the radius $R(t)$ for $0 <= t <= 3$. Use your expression to find $R(3)$.

(b) Find the rate at which the cross-sectional area $A(t)$ is increasing at time $t = 3$ years. Indicate units of measure.

(c) Evaluate $integral_(0)^(3) A'(t) d t$. Using appropriate units, interpret the meaning of that integral in terms of cross- sectional area.
